description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
Random init; prints the task's attributes and method signatures to learn the prompt/answer format.
d_model=1, no LayerNorm: uniform attention counts the 1s, then 10 ReLU kinks form a triangle wave of the count (+1 odd, -1 even).
Same count circuit, but the residual supplies the first slope, so only 9 ReLU kinks are needed (ten segments for ten sign changes).
Lower-bound probe: only 8 ReLU kinks, one too few for ten sign changes. NOT actually perfect: exhaustive check is 2045/2046 (min_margin -3); the 200-sample eval misses the failing all-ones input.
Attention counts the 1s, then 4 blocks of one ReLU each fold the number line (x -> |x| - a). Bug: '=' offset -5 was double counted through attention and the residual, giving c-10 (exhaustive 0.3113).
FoldDepth4 with the offset fixed ('=' -> -5/2, counted by both attention and the residual): 4 one-ReLU blocks fold x -> |x| - a.
FoldDepth4Fixed with the position embedding deleted: parity is order-invariant, so positions carry no information.
FoldNoPosEmb with attention only in the first block: one attention layer to count, then three attention-free fold blocks.
One attention layer counts the 1s, then a single tied ReLU block x -> |x| - 1 is applied five times; head bias centres the {-1, 0} result.
TiedFold5 without head bias: even counts give all-zero logits and rely on argmax breaking ties toward index 0. Fragile by design (margin 0).
TiedFold5 shifted to half-integer coordinates, so the fold's fixed points are +/-1/2: the same 16 params as the argmax-tie version, but with a real 0.5 margin and no head bias.
Non-standard activation: one layer and one cos unit compute cos(pi * count), so depth and folding are unnecessary. Same 16 params as the fold, margin 1.
Unmodified stock architecture (64d, 4 heads, 3 layers, LayerNorm, pos_emb): large fixed anchor dims make LayerNorm nearly linear, so the count-plus-triangle circuit survives.
Stock component types (LayerNorm, pos_emb) at the smallest size: d_model=4 (s, -s, A, -A), 1 head, 1 layer, 9 hidden units, A=1000.
AnchoredD4 sensitivity sweep: anchor A=30 is too small. Exhaustive 0.9726 (min_margin -1.05): count drift is about c^3/(2A^2), which needs A > sqrt(1000) = 31.6.

AnchoredD4 sensitivity sweep: A=40. NOT actually perfect: exhaustive 2045/2046 (min_margin -0.19); the 200-sample eval misses it. Predicted a pass, but the residual keeps the true count, so drift counts twice and A > 44.7 is needed.
AnchoredD4 sensitivity sweep: A=50, above the corrected threshold A > 44.7 (drift counted twice via the residual). Exhaustive 2046/2046, min_margin 0.11 (predicted about 0.2).
No MLP: softmax is the only nonlinearity. Attention counts the 1s, then a quadratic attention score addresses position t = count and reads its stored parity from pos_emb.
All 16 weights are integers: the state Y = 2c - 9 stays an odd integer, the fold is Y -> |Y - 1| - 1, and the fixed points +/-1 give margin 1.

Depth probe: only 3 of the 5 folds. Exhaustive matches the hand prediction exactly (1980/2046 = 0.9677; c=1 and c=9 fail). Eval is lower because it appears to oversample short strings, where c=1 is common.
Depth probe: 7 folds. Once at the fixed points, +1 and -1 swap on each step, so two extra folds should change nothing while the head stays the same.

Robustness measurement of TiedFold5Integer: N(0, 0.05) noise on every weight, 20 seeds, each scored on all 2046 prompts: 5/20 perfect, mean 0.8992, min 0.2903. The 0.56 is one noisy seed, not the clean model.
Robustness measurement of CosineCount with the same protocol as TiedFoldNoise05: 5/20 perfect, mean 0.7971, min 0.0655. The 0.485 is one noisy seed, not the clean model.
Digital finite-state machine: layer i reads bit i by address into a register, and one shared steep-ReLU XOR gate updates s ^= r, snapping s to {0, 1} each layer. 10 layers.

Robustness measurement of ScanAutomaton with the same protocol: 0/20 perfect, mean 0.4531, min 0.0630. Confounded: noising structurally zero weights penalises model size, so this does not show the digital design is worse.

Fairer robustness protocol for ScanAutomaton: N(0, 0.05) only on nonzero weights, 20 seeds, all 2046 prompts: 11/20 perfect, mean 0.7863, min 0.3558, mostly bimodal. The 0.73 is one noisy seed, not the clean model.

Fairer robustness protocol for TiedFold5Integer: N(0, 0.05) only on nonzero weights, 20 seeds, all 2046 prompts: 7/20 perfect, mean 0.9291, min 0.5000, degrades gradually. The 0.78 is one noisy seed, not the clean model.

Fairer robustness protocol for CosineCount: N(0, 0.05) only on nonzero weights, 20 seeds, all 2046 prompts: 12/20 perfect, mean 0.8667, min 0.2737. The 1.0 is one lucky noisy seed, not a robustness result.
Recommended model, re-verified clean: 16 integer weights, one attention layer counts the 1s, one tied ReLU block folds Y -> |Y - 1| - 1 five times.
